title: Aggregate RRC is built bottom-up from three per-risk components summed per Instance, then across Instances
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.1.1 defines the composition in two steps. Instance Total RRC "is the sum of all applicable risk-specific RRC calculations for that Instance," listing Instance Financial RRC, Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC. Aggregate RRC per Prime Agent "is the sum of all its Instance Total RRCs" and is "the figure against which a Prime Agent's Total Risk Capital (TRC) adequacy is assessed."

The decomposition by *risk type* is the substantive choice. It separates the risk that a position loses value, the risk that the code holding it fails, and the risk that whoever operates it errs — three causes with different mitigations and different modelling maturity. A single blended charge would hide which one is driving a requirement, and could not be improved piecewise.

Strict additivity is the second choice, and it is deliberately conservative: no diversification credit is given for holding several Instances or for offsetting exposures. This makes the figure trivially auditable and removes an entire class of correlation-modelling disputes, at the price of overstating capital needs for a genuinely diversified book.

Summing to *one* number per Prime is what lets everything downstream be simple. The OVRC monitor, the penalty accrual, the internal alerting and the TRC Report's capital buffer all compare against the same scalar, so "adequate" has exactly one meaning across automated and human enforcement.
description: Instance Total RRC sums Financial, Smart Contract and Administrative RRC; Aggregate RRC sums those, giving one figure that is both risk-decomposed and the single test of TRC adequacy.
